# Scope
In scope
• Sales ASN creation against a sales order, for Article and Kit
• ASN type check (With GDN / Without GDN) and the company setting check
• FG allocation tab (site, stock qty, stock type) on the Sales ASN
• Validation on confirm, auto stock entry and auto stock transfer out
• Traceability of the posted stock to the ASN and its sales order
Out of scope
• The normal "With GDN" ASN flow (unchanged)
• Order-confirmation (OC) linked stock allocation; this flow creates free stock only
• Changes to the sales order module

# Purpose
Finished goods need to be dispatched from the warehouse, but the stock isn’t in the system’s inventory, so a normalGDN-based dispatch can’t be made.

# Solution

## Sales ASN
A new system setting, “FG Allocation without GDN”, enables a stock-less dispatch flow in the Sales ASN. When the setting is ON and the ASN Type is Without GDN, the FG Allocation tab is shown on the ASN. The user enters the Site and the stock quantity to allocate, with stock type Free (not linked to any OC). When the user confirms the sales ASN, the system automatically raises two transactions using the Site and quantity from the FG Allocation tab:
• Enter New Stock: brings the free stock into the selected Site.
• Transfer Out of System: moves the same stock out of the system against the ASN.
The goods are dispatched without existing inventory, with no manual stock entries, no leftover stock, and full traceability to the ASN and its sales order. The whole flow is switched on or off by the one setting.

### Business Workflow

### Sales ASN workflow: FG allocation without GDN
• Sales order created. The sales order is created in the Sales module. Its open order deliveries are the base for the ASN.
• Sales ASN created against the sales order. The user raises a new ASN (ASN For: Article or Kit), chooses the Buyer and adds the open order deliveries through the Select Order picker (S-1a).
• ASN Type check. With GDN: the FG Allocation tab is shown by default and the normal ASN flow applies; no automatic stock transactions are raised. Without GDN: the setting decides (step 4).
• Setting check, “FG Allocation without GDN”. ON: the FG Allocation tab is added to the ASN. OFF: no FG Allocation tab; the ASN works as a standard ASN and no stock transactions are raised.
• FG allocation entry. In the FG Allocation tab the user enters the Site and the quantity to allocate (Trf. GDI Qty) on each row. Stock Type is Free, not linked to any OC.
• Confirm sales ASN. The user confirms the ASN (V-2, V-3). The automatic transactions are controlled by the setting.
• Automatic stock transactions. For each Site the system raises Enter New Stock, then Transfer Out of System, using the Site and quantity from the FG Allocation tab, in the same action as the Confirm.
• Sales ASN confirmed. The ASN gets its Shipment No., becomes read-only, and the confirmation banner lists the stock transaction numbers.

### Scenarios

[TABLE 2: Table 2 · 3 rows · columns: ASN Type (text), Setting “FG Allocation without GDN” (text), FG Allocation tab (text), Automatic stock transactions on Confirm (text)]
| ASN Type | Setting “FG Allocation without GDN” | FG Allocation tab | Automatic stock transactions on Confirm |
| With GDN | not used | Shown by default | None, normal ASN flow |
| Without GDN | ON | Shown | Enter New Stock, then Transfer Out of System (when at least one row has a Site and Trf. GDI Qty above 0) |
| Without GDN | OFF | Hidden | None, standard ASN |
FG Allocation tab for an ASN Without GDN
Note: screen will be in 4.0 this is just for reference.
In this case stock type column will always be free.

## Auto generated transaction
The transactions shall be generated based on the number of distinct sites selected in the FG Allocation tab, subject to the following conditions:
• Multiple distinct sites: If FG Allocation contains entries for four different sites, the system shall automatically generate four separate Enter New Stock transactions and four separate Transfer Out of System transactions, with each transaction corresponding to its respective site.
• Single site with multiple rows: If FG Allocation contains four rows for the same site, differentiated by color and size, the system shall generate only one Enter New Stock transaction and one Transfer Out of System transaction for that site. The transaction details shall include the applicable color-wise and size-wise stock entries.

## Transaction Generation Logic
The system shall determine the number of transactions to generate based on the distinct sites present in the FG Allocation tab.

[TABLE 7: Table 7 · 3 rows · columns: Scenario (text), FG Allocation Details (text), Enter New Stock Transactions (integer), Transfer Out of System Transactions (integer)]
| Scenario | FG Allocation Details | Enter New Stock Transactions | Transfer Out of System Transactions |
| Scenario 1 | Four rows belonging to four distinct sites | 4 | 4 |
| Scenario 2 | Four rows belonging to one site, with different color/size combinations | 1 | 1 |
| Scenario 3 | Multiple rows distributed across two distinct sites | 2 | 2 |
For each distinct site, the system shall create one Enter New Stock transaction and one corresponding Transfer Out of System transaction. The applicable color-wise, size-wise and stock quantity details shall be populated from the Sales ASN.
